name: Two Queens, One King — Probability Explained
html:
Joint probability · Card draws
Two Queens, One King
Drawing 4 cards from a standard deck — working out the joint probability, then turning it into a short.
Part 1 · Work the problem
The givens
52
Deck
Standard, 52 cards
4
Draw
4 cards
X = 2
Queens
exactly two
Y = 1
Kings
exactly one
$$f_{XY}(2,\,1)\;=\;?$$
Step 1
Total possible outcomes
The number of ways to draw any 4 cards from 52 is a straightforward combination.
$$\binom{52}{4} = \frac{52!}{4!(52-4)!} = 270{,}725$$
Step 2
Favourable outcomes
$$\begin{aligned}\text{The Queens}\quad &\binom{4}{2} = 6 \\ \text{The King}\quad &\binom{4}{1} = 4 \\ \text{The last card}\quad &\binom{44}{1} = 44\end{aligned}$$
The last card must be neither Queen nor King, leaving 52 − 4 − 4 = 44 safe cards.
Step 3
Putting it together
Multiply the favourable combinations and divide by the total.
$$\text{Probability} = \frac{\binom{4}{2} \times \binom{4}{1} \times \binom{44}{1}}{\binom{52}{4}}$$
The numbers
$$= \frac{6 \times 4 \times 44}{270{,}725} = \frac{1{,}056}{270{,}725}$$
1,056
winning hands, out of 270,725 possible
6 queen pairs4 kings44 others
Answer
≈ 0.0039
0.39%
of all four-card hands succeed
roughly 1 hand in 256matches option B
